paragraphs.text: Right-to-left (Persian/Arabic/Hebrew) text support for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI: per-block bidi d
irection, LTR code, logical list and quote geometry.
# DeepSeek Harness RTL

A DeepSeek Harness bundle that
makes right-to-left content (Persian/Farsi, Arabic, Hebrew) render co

rrectly in
the Web UI — including messages that mix RTL text with English words,
identifiers, filena
mes and inline code.

A plugin bundle for the `desktop`/Web profile. No build step, no dependencies,
no Host services: a s
tylesheet and a small DOM observer in the browser half.
## The problem

The Harness shell is authored left-to-right: no stylesheet sets `direction` and
no element carries a

`dir` attribute. Every message therefore inherits an LTR
paragraph level, so Persian text shows up

` attribute. Every message therefore inherits an LTR
paragraph level, so Persian text shows up with:

- wrong alignment (ragged-right lines packed to the left),
- list markers and block-quote bars on th

e wrong side, sometimes overlapping text,
- sentence-final punctuation on the wrong end,
- mixed Per
sian/English lines that read in the wrong order.
## What it does
| Layer | Behaviour |
| Paragraph direction | Each paragraph, list item, heading, quote and table cell resolves its own ba

se direction (UAX #9 first-strong), so RTL and LTR paragraphs coexist in one message. |
| Alignment

| Blocks align to their *resolved* direction instead of the inherited one. |
| Mixed lines | A block
that *starts* with an English term but is otherwise Persian (`` - `useState`: وضعیت کامپوننت ``) is

pinned to RTL by a majority heuristic instead of being read left-to-right. |
| Code | `pre`, `code`
, `kbd`, `samp` and code-block chrome are forced LTR and isolated, so snippets, paths and shell comm

ands inside a Persian sentence never re-order. |
| Logical geometry | List indentation, block-quote
bars and task-list checkboxes use `inline-start/end`, so RTL lists keep their markers on the right w

ithout overlapping text. |
| Composer | Plain inputs/textareas get `dir="auto"`; the Lexical editor
already applies it to its editable roots. |

Only transcript and Markdown surfaces are affected (`[data-chat-flow]`,
`[class*="_markdown_"]`); si

debars, settings and other chrome keep their LTR
layout.
## Before / after

Left: the current behaviour — Persian lines left-aligned, markers on the left,
quote bar on the left

, mixed lines out of order. Right: the same document with
this bundle installed.

The bundle inserts one Loader row (`rtl-bidi`) after the profile's other
bundles. Reload the page on

ce after installing; the stylesheet and observer are
attached when the Client module boots. Disable

or remove it from
**Settings → Plugins** at any time.
## Verifying the rendering

`test/fixture.html` reproduces the transcript DOM and the relevant shipped
Markdown CSS; `test/compa

re.html` shows both states side by side. With a
Chromium-based browser:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`--dump-dom` on the same URL shows the pinned blocks:
`data-dsh-dir="rtl"` on Persian blocks, `data-

dsh-dir="ltr"` on English ones,
and no attribute on blocks that only contain digits or punctuation.
## Known limits

- Direction is decided per block with the first-strong heuristic plus a
Persian-majority override. A

deliberately English-first sentence that
mentions one Persian word stays left-to-right.
- Markdown

tables keep left-to-right column order; cell text is aligned per cell.
- Rendering uses the browser'

s fallback font for Arabic-script glyphs; the
bundle does not ship or select a Persian font.
- Block
s that only contain digits/punctuation keep the surrounding direction.
## Development

`client.js` is a prebuilt browser module in the platform's
`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, facto

ry })` format — there is no compile
step. Edit it, then reload the page; a locally linked install pi

cks up the new
file directly.

The stylesheet is a template string near the top of the module, so it stays in
source order (prose r

ules, then code rules, then the pinned-direction rule that
wins over the heuristic).
